pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision... — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
At Tufnell Park, every child flourishes into a resourceful, resilient and responsible citizen, developing the knowledge, skills and attributes required to thrive in the wider world.
Children experience a rich, purposeful and balanced curriculum, enhanced by a range of cultural, artistic, sporting, civic and real-life experiences to broaden their horizons, through the Tufnell Park Promise. Staff and pupils strive for excellence in all areas, leading to the school becoming the first choice for parents in the area.
Our school community have identified two particular aspects of learning to prepare our children for future success. The intention is that all children become:
Tufnell Park children are skilled and discerning users of technology, developing their own creativity and ingenuity to enhance their learning and solve real world questions and problems
We will achieve this through:
Tufnell Park children are passionate, knowledgeable advocates for the natural environment, for sustainable practices, and for healthy, active lifestyles
We will achieve this through:

At Tufnell Park Primary we value:
…the range of talent and ability in every child. Our school’s primary aim is to identify the full breadth of each pupil’s capabilities and develop these to their best advantage, for life.
…the extraordinary potential of our pupils. We believe that, whatever their level of ambition, children can achieve even more than anyone at first imagines. We aim to provide the opportunity and support always to go further.
…love of learning as a source of joy and achievement. By example and through nurture, we seek at all times to encourage lively, enquiring minds. Our aim is to produce pupils who enjoy and welcome challenge, because challenge is an adventure they are equipped to meet.
…self confidence founded on self worth and reinforced through success. We aim for all our children to develop a justified sense of self assurance to help them pursue their life goals with a good heart and an open mind.
…a sense of belonging and enabling others to belong. We aim for our school to be a happy, inviting place where people treat one another with kindness, tolerance and respect, and variety is celebrated.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our latest results 2023 — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
What amazing results! We are so proud!
Our end of key stage results this year are FANTASTIC! We are above Islington and national averages in every measure, in every subject and at every level. That means whatever age and whatever level of achievement they are working at, children at Tufnell Park do at least as well as those of our local neighbours, and significantly better than most children in the country.
Our progress scores are significantly above national averages, putting us firmly in the top 10% of schools for a number of years running now.
Well done everyone – your amazing hard work and commitment to learning has really paid off.

pageCache.pageTitle: PTA General Meeting – 2 Oct — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Looking for a New PTA Chair
On 2 October, we will be looking for a new Chair of the Tufnell Park Primary School PTA. We will be holding a General Meeting earlier than our Annual General Meeting so that there is time to plan for the Panto and Winter Fair.
Below is an overview of the responsibilities of the Chair.
Strategy and school partnership
The Chair provides overall leadership and direction for the PTA. They work closely with the school, elected committee and core parent-volunteers to coordinate the PTA’s activities, identify priorities and help ensure that the time and money contributed by parents are translated into positive outcomes for the school and its children.
Working with the elected committee, core parent-volunteers and the school, the Chair helps define the PTA’s priorities and strategy for the year. This can include identifying funding priorities and potential projects, planning fundraising activities, seeking corporate sponsorship and helping coordinate the implementation of PTA-supported initiatives.
The Chair acts as an important point of contact between the PTA and the school, helping ensure that PTA activities and investments are aligned with the school’s priorities.
Fundraising and community events
Community events and fundraising are an important part of the PTA’s activities. Historically, the Chair has led the organising and coordination of the Winter Fair, Summer Fair and Fun Run. Last year, the school also hosted the Panto, with the PTA running the concessions.
The Chair works with parent-volunteers and school staff who are taking responsibility for different aspects of these events to help bring the overall programme together.
Governance and finances
Tufnell Park Primary School PTA is a registered charity and therefore requires appropriate governance and financial oversight.
Working closely with the Treasurer and other trustees, the Chair helps oversee the PTA’s finances and reviews and approves minor budget requests, including bursaries, the Science Fair, Black History Month and Smart Swap needs. For larger funding requests, the Chair works closely with the school, elected committee members and core parent-volunteers to consider priorities and agree how PTA funds should be allocated.
The Chair also helps ensure that the appropriate records and information are prepared for the AGM and annual regulatory filings.
Communications and resources
The Chair works closely with the Head of Communications to develop the PTA’s communications priorities for each term and ensure that parents and the wider school community are kept informed about PTA activities, events and opportunities to become involved.
The Chair also works closely with and supports the Head of Resources to ensure that the PTA has the equipment and materials needed for upcoming activities and that its existing resources are maintained and managed sustainably.
Building the PTA community
An important part of the Chair role is helping parents become involved in the PTA. The Chair works with committee members and core volunteers to identify opportunities for participation, connect volunteers with activities where they can contribute, and help build a strong and sustainable parent-volunteer community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enhancing the playground for play and learning — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Developing a unified strategy for outdoor play and learning
Building on existing parent and school initiatives in this area, we are now taking the important step of developing a unified Outdoor Play and Learning Strategy for the school.
This work is an important part of realising the school’s vision that children become passionate, knowledgeable advocates for the natural environment, sustainable practices, and healthy, active lifestyles.
In support of the school’s vision, the strategy will be a coordinated plan to help the school set and achieve measurable goals for improving access to and use of its outdoor spaces. It will support integration of time spent outside into children’s days, and identify ways that our outdoor space could be enhanced to improve children’s play and learning experiences. It will also provide a resource for fundraising.
The strategy will consist of three sections, mirroring the three stages of the process
We are currently nearing the end of the information-gathering stage, and look forward to incorporating responses to the parent survey as we identify projects in the second stage of work. The strategy is being led by Anne Jaluzot – Green infrastructure planning consultant, in collaboration with the school, the PTA, and other parents with expertise and enthusiasm in this area.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Curriculum — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Developing pupil’s independence and motivation as learners, and as resourceful, resilient and responsible citizens is at the heart of all our teaching and learning.
For more information on the thinking behind our curriculum, see our Curriculum Statement page.
For information on how we structure and support our youngest children’s learning, visit our EYFS homepage.
To see our AMAZING results for the end of last year (2023) click here.
For subject specific information, please click on the buttons below.
Though not National Curriculum subjects, our curriculum also places focus on these specific areas – click below for more information.
Remote Education
This Policy was developed in response to Covid related absences and closures during 2020-21. Remote learning will be shared with families in line with the policy below, during Covid related closure/absence, or other long term absence.
Remote Education Policy

Autumn Term clubs run from w/c 23rd September 24 to w/c 2nd December 2024 (unless it is a Friday club which finish on 9th December 2024)
Spring Term clubs run from w/c 13th January 2025 to w/c 24th March 2025
Summer Term clubs run from 28th April 2025 to w/c 7th July 2025 (unless it is a Monday club which may finish 14th July 2025)
Tufnell Park have a wide rang of enrichment clubs Monday through to Friday. Parents will be emailed on Teachers2Parents with a MonkeySurvey link for the 3 key stages. Each child needs an individual form completing. The offers then go out the week before clubs start. Within a few weeks a SchoolMoney payment will be set up for each child who accepts their place. Please ensure that the office has your current email address otherwise you may miss the link email.
The cost for a 10-week term is still £30.00. Please ensure your payments are kept up to date.
Any questions, please email: parentmail@tufnellpark.islington.sch.uk
We’re very proud of the range of clubs we offer to children from Year 1 upwards. We want our children to have a wide range of experiences and challenge themselves to try lots of activities whilst they are at our school.
There are clubs for different sports, arts and skills. We hope there is something for everyone and encourage all children to do at least one club.
What we offer varies somewhat from term to term, depending on the tutors available and demand from the children. Most are oversubscribed but we rotate membership so that as many children as possible get their chance over the course of the year. You can indicate your child’s interest in a club by signing up towards the end of each term. Offer letters will go out as soon as possible.
We do our best to keep charges extremely low. The charge is currently £30 for a term which is usually 10 sessions – that’s only £3.00 per session! Payments are taken online or you can use childcare vouchers/tax free childcare.
Please make sure that you arrive at school promptly to pick up your child when their club finishes- clubs run from 3.30 to 4.30. Children that are picked up continually late may lose their place at their chosen club.
If you have any questions about clubs, please email: parentmail@tufnellpark.islington.sch.uk.
Please note that these clubs are an opportunity for children to pursue their interests and acquire new ones. The availability of clubs changes over the year so they should not be considered as regular child care provision.

pageCache.pageTitle: School Games Award — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
We are delighted to announce that we, Tufnell Park Primary School, have achieved the School Games GOLD Mark Award for the 2025/26 academic year.
The School Games Mark is a Government-led award scheme launched in 2012, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust to reward schools for their commitment to the development of competition across their school and into the community, and we are delighted to have been recognised for our success.
Our sporting achievements this year include:some fantastic results in the swimming gala, cross country and building girls participation across all sports.
With a total of young people competing in local inter-school competitions this year, we are extremely proud of our pupils for their dedication to all aspects of school sport, including those young volunteers, leaders and officials who made our competitions possible.
As part of our application, we were asked to fulfil criteria in the areas of participation, competition, workforce and clubs, and we are pleased that the hard work of everyone at our school has been rewarded this year.
A special thanks to:All our amazing children, the PTA and all our staff.
We look forward to applying once again in 2027!

pageCache.pageTitle: Choosing Tufnell Park Primary — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Tufnell Park! I am extremely proud to be headteacher of this vibrant and exciting school. We pride ourselves on being a school that reflects our local community in all its diversity. We all bring a wide variety of experience and knowledge to Tufnell Park, and celebrate and draw strength from that. Children learn that we must not only tolerate and respect difference, but that there are huge benefits in learning from one another. Ours is a school where parents, children and staff value the opportunity to work together for the benefit of all. And together, we certainly deliver – see our fantastic results here!
In September 2019, we moved into a stunning brand new building, with expanded state of the art facilities and landscaped grounds reflecting the high aspirations we hold for our community. Our site on the brow of a hill gives wonderful views across North London—big skies and wide horizons are always in evidence. We are surrounded by natural wildlife spaces and mature trees, so we are able to enjoy a peaceful and containing space that brings us close to nature, whilst still being only minutes away from the heart of London and all that offers.
Our curriculum has been designed with inclusivity at its heart to raise aspirations and give all pupils appropriate experiences to ensure they become resourceful, resilient and responsible citizens, ready to lead successful lives at secondary school and beyond. We are a good school—children make rapid progress and achieve highly in core learning, as our results show. However, we also strive to ensure that rich, relevant and well-planned experiences across the breadth of our entire curriculum lead to deep learning and the development of character and good learning habits. We strive to make our curriculum a place where children and can discover and develop their particular abilities and talents, whatever they might be.
Our school community has identified two particular aspects of learning to prepare our children for future success. The intention is that all our children become skilled and discerning users of technology, and passionate, knowledgeable advocates for the natural environment, for sustainable practices, and for healthy, active lifestyles. You can read more about this in our vision statement and school promise.
At Tufnell Park Primary, we are all on a learning journey—children, parents and staff alike—with a shared expectation that we should be improving all the time. We are committed to being the best school that we can possibly be, and also to the success and happiness of those in our community. We would love for you to accompany us on our exciting journey.
Martin ScarboroughHeadteacher

“What a lovely school this is!” enthused Miss Noel Streatfield, a renowned children’s author of the time, as she opened Tufnell Park School in 1955. “So modern.”
Gothic houses along Carleton Road were razed to make way for a purpose-built school for the children growing up on the new Hilldrop and Tufnell Park estates. The development was clearly welcome: according to the local paper, the queue of families waiting to enrol stretched round the corner. The school opened with 350 children taught by just nine teachers and the headmistress, Mrs Kemp.
Our school has continued to serve the area, and the children from Hilldrop and Tufnell Park estates, for almost 60 years. The 1980s saw the demolition of the keeper’s house to be replaced by the school pond—now part of our extensive wild garden. In 2005, a major building project introduced premises for our nursery, bringing it on site for the first time.
Throughout our continuing evolution, the sentiments of the first Assistant Head—one Alderman Lendon—still hold true:
“The children are certainly enthusiastic,” he said, as the school opened.
“There is no doubt we shall all get along very well together.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Nursery admissions — Tufnell Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
2 year olds
In September 2019, we moved into our new building, and opened a brand new provision for 2 year olds.
Children can be admitted in the term after their second birthday:
These are 15 hour places, term time only, Monday to Friday, morning or afternoon. See below for information on free early education for 2 year olds and details of our charges if you are not eligible for the free 15 hours.
If you wish to apply, please download and complete the attached form 1b-2-YO-Nursery-Application-Form-2022-23-1 and bring it to the school office along with your child’s birth certificate or passport. We will also need proof of address (for you and your child).
Please get in touch if you’d like to know more by emailing us.
We will follow the Islington admissions procedure: Tufnell Park School Nursery admissions policy
How to get 15 hours free early education (2 year olds)
Find out if you are eligible for 15 hours free 2 year old early education here: http://www.islington.gov.uk/free2
If you receive an ‘eligibility code’ , please the Parent Declaration Form so that we can receive the funding for your child’s place. Parent Declaration Form
3 and 4 year olds
We offer part-time and full-time places:
Our 15 hour sessions are Monday-Friday (term time only) first half of the week (Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday morning) OR second half of the week (Wednesday afternoon, Thursday and Friday).
Our 30 hour places are Monday-Friday (term time only) from 9.00am to 3.25pm.
Children can be admitted in the term after their third birthday:
All 3-4 year olds are entitled to 15 hours free early education. Working families may be entitled to 30 hours. See below for more information and our charges.
If you wish to apply for a place, please download and complete the attached application form 1a-3-4-YO-Nursery-Application-Form-2022-23-1 and bring it to the school office along with your child’s birth certificate or passport. We will also need proof of address (for you and your child).
It is also important to stress that acceptance to our Nursery class does not ensure a place in the main school. Please see how to apply for a Reception place in our school here: Admissions (Reception to Year 6)
If you would like to visit our 3-4 year old nursery, please call the main school office on 020 7607 4852 or email us.
How to get 15 or 30 hours free early education (3-4 year olds)
All 3 and 4 year olds are entitled to 15 hours free early learning.
To get the free 15 hours, you do not need to do anything except complete the Parent Declaration Form so that we can receive the funding for your child’s place. Parent Declaration From
Many working families are eligible for 30 hours per week.
If you would like 30 hours and are working parent(s) you can apply for an ‘eligibility code’ here: https://www.gov.uk/apply-30-hours-free-tax-free-childcare
When you have your eligibility code, please write this on your Parent Declaration Form.
PARENTS CAN PAY FOR ADDITIONAL HOURS
Parents can pay for additional hours, we follow the Islington Early Years Childcare Charging Policy. To find out more information please click this link.
https://www.islington.gov.uk/~/media/sharepoint-lists/public-records/childrenandfamiliesservices/information/leaflets/20252026/islington-early-years-charging-policy-september-2025.pdf
Islington Council may also be able to help if you if you don’t qualify for the above schemes but are just starting work or in training which will lead to work. The Childcare Bursary could provide short-term support – find out more here: www.islington.gov.uk/children-and-families/benefits-and-financial-support/childcare-bursary
Government tax-free childcare and other help with paying for childcare
The Best Start in Life website is a great place to find out all the different types of childcare support available to you, depending on the age of your child and your circumstances:
https://beststartinlife.gov.uk
There is lots more information about support with childcare and about childcare providers on the Islington Family Information Service website: http://www.islington.gov.uk/fis

Tufnell Park Primary School’s PTA is a parents and carers group whose aim is to enrich the experience your children have during their time at the school, by providing useful and fun events and experiences that the school cannot provide (for whatever reason).
Our activities are all about funds AND fun, bringing the school community together is one of our most important purposes.
If you have a child at the school, congratulations, you are already a PTA member! It’s up to you how much you can contribute, and you are free to get involved with anything we are doing, whatever the age of your child. You will always be welcomed and helping out may be much easier than you think. Whether it is baking for a cake sale, looking after a stall at the Summer Fair or taking up a post on the Committee – your contributions and support are invaluable in making the PTA a worthwhile part of school life.
The PTA is run by a committee that is voted in each Autumn, If you are interested in being part of it, please come to our Annual General Meeting and raise your hand – no experience is necessary. The Committee meets about twice a term and you can read the reports of those meetings here. When we are planning an event, such as the Winter Wonderland or Summer Fair, every member of the school is encouraged to join in. PLEASE come and help plan: we literally can’t do it without you! And if you’ve ever got a question or an idea about anything at all – how things are organised, how to get involved, something you’d like to run yourself – please drop us a line or say “Hello” in the playground.
For more information about what the PTA does and who the current committee members are, please click here
